topic: Promise.all vs Promise.allSettled: one rejection hides every other result, and the other operations keep running
text:
One failed request shouldn't hide the nine that worked.

Promise.all rejects on the first rejection and throws away the other results. Per MDN, it also doesn't cancel the remaining operations: they keep running, you just can't see their outcome.

Promise.allSettled waits for every promise and returns { status, value | reason } for each, in input order.

My rule of thumb:
• Tasks depend on each other → Promise.all
• You need every outcome (batch jobs, dashboards, bulk emails) → Promise.allSettled

Fail-fast is a feature when the whole result is useless without every part. It's a bug when partial success is still valuable.

Where do you still reach for Promise.all out of habit when allSettled would be the safer default?
